question: Can grokking in nonlinear networks be derived from gradient dynamics as a staged feature-emergence process, with provable sample-size boundaries between generalizable group features and memorization?

key_findings.claim: The Li2 framework divides grokking into lazy top-layer fitting, independent hidden-feature learning, and interactive feature refinement, with the backpropagated hidden-activation gradient linking the stages.
key_findings.evidence: During lazy learning the output layer fits labels using random hidden features while creating a label-correlated gradient G_F. Each hidden node then initially follows a decoupled update; after hidden activations become correlated, feature repulsion and top-down modulation couple the nodes.

key_findings.claim: Independent feature learning is exactly gradient ascent on a nonlinear CCA energy whose local maxima identify emergent features.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 gives E(w_j)=one-half norm-squared of centered label features transposed against sigma(Xw_j). For quadratic activations on finite-group arithmetic, Theorem 2 characterizes every local maximum as paired vectors inside real or complex irreducible-representation subspaces and states that no other local maxima exist.

key_findings.claim: For group tasks, a complete set of irreducible-representation features can reconstruct the centered target with far fewer hidden units than pairwise memorization.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3 reconstructs the target given a basis of learned rank-one matrices. In an Abelian group it requires K=2M-2 units, compared with M-squared units for a construction that stores every input pair; the theorem relies on complex-domain optimization or a real-domain perturbation supplied by later interaction.

key_findings.claim: The proposed generalization boundary is a stability threshold of the feature-energy landscape under sampling.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4 states that on the order of d_k squared times M log(M/delta) uniformly sampled group pairs preserves the local maximum for a d_k-dimensional irrep. For modular addition this yields a training fraction on the order of log(M)/M; Figure 5 reports a sharp empirical zero-to-one test-accuracy transition near the predicted boundary.

key_findings.claim: Interactive learning supplies a mechanism for feature diversity and a first-principles interpretation of Muon's usefulness.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 6 derives repulsion between nodes with similar activations; Theorem 7 states that after a subset of group features is learned the top-layer residual gradient emphasizes missing features; Theorem 8 argues that Muon's matrix update rebalances singular directions and thereby improves diversity relative to unnormalized gradient flow.

key_findings.claim: Weight decay is sufficient but not necessary for grokking in this framework, and it acts as an effective feature-learning rate in the late lazy solution.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion relates the asymptotic hidden gradient to weight decay and recovers a time scale proportional to its inverse. It also explains that any mechanism preserving a nonzero label-correlated G_F, such as slower top-layer overfitting, can initiate feature learning without explicit regularization.

method.core_idea: Track the backpropagated gradient into hidden activations and use its changing algebraic structure to derive successive regimes of grokking rather than fitting a phenomenological test-loss curve.
method.mechanism: The output layer first approaches a ridge-like solution over near-random hidden features. Its residual produces a label-correlated hidden gradient that decouples across nodes and equals ascent on a nonlinear CCA energy. Finite-group representation theory solves the energy landscape; concentration bounds determine when sampled data preserves its generalizable maxima. Later correlations introduce cross-node repulsion and residual-driven emphasis on missing irreps.
assumptions: The most explicit landscape and sample-complexity results assume group-arithmetic inputs and principally a quadratic activation.
The main derivation studies a two-layer nonlinear model before outlining an extension to deeper networks.
Hidden-feature stages are separated sufficiently for the approximate gradients used in each regime to dominate.
Target reconstruction uses a complete collection of learned irrep features and, in its exact form, complex-valued optimization.

techniques.role: Separates training by the changing structure of gradients reaching the hidden layer.
Turns individual hidden-node dynamics into ascent on an interpretable scalar feature objective.
Enumerates generalizable local maxima for group arithmetic via representation theory.
Uses concentration to derive the data threshold at which population features survive empirical sampling.
Explains how interacting nodes diversify and redirect capacity toward still-missing features.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer networks on modular addition for several group sizes, data fractions, widths, initializations, and optimizers; primary plots average 15 seeds.
evaluations.metric: Training/test accuracy, feature alignment, gradient structure, and location of the generalization phase boundary.
evaluations.result: The empirical transition from non-generalizing to generalizing solutions tracks the predicted training fraction proportional to log(M)/M, and Fourier features emerge in the staged order described by Li2.
evaluations.baseline: Direct numerical training dynamics compared with theorem-predicted energy maxima and phase boundaries.

evaluations.setting: Small-data modular arithmetic and optimizer comparisons including gradient descent and Muon.
evaluations.metric: Diversity of learned frequencies, persistence of generalizable basins, and generalization speed.
evaluations.result: The experiments support the predicted feature repulsion, top-down focus on missing modes, and improved feature diversity under Muon, while showing that excessive learning rates can escape the remaining generalizable basins in scarce-data regimes.
evaluations.baseline: Standard gradient dynamics without the corresponding interaction or matrix-normalization effect.

limitations: Author-stated: although the energy derivation accepts arbitrary inputs, its local-maxima analysis relies on restrictive group structure.
Author-stated: the work does not derive transition times between the three learning stages.
The exact feature catalogue emphasizes quadratic activations and shallow networks, far from the normalization, attention, and cross-entropy dynamics of production language models.
The reconstruction theorem needs a strong coverage assumption over irrep features and an exact complex-domain form that real networks only approximate after interaction.
Most validation uses modular arithmetic, so the claimed extension to complex structured inputs remains principally a mathematical program rather than broad empirical evidence.
failure_modes: Non-group data may yield an energy landscape with unstructured or spurious maxima that do not correspond to reusable features.
Stages may overlap, invalidating the independent-node approximation before useful maxima are reached.
Limited data can deform the landscape so memorizing directions have higher energy than population features.
Very large width can shrink the per-node hidden gradient and return training toward an effectively lazy regime.
An optimizer may alter the gradient geometry in ways not represented by the proposed continuous-time approximations.
reusable_insights: Analyze emergent capabilities by the gradient signal delivered to a representation layer, not only by external loss curves.
View data thresholds as stability of useful feature optima under finite sampling.
Use symmetries to turn otherwise opaque nonconvex feature landscapes into a finite, testable catalogue.
Separate initial output-layer overfitting from later memorizing features; both look like memorization but have different mechanisms.
Test optimizer claims through their effect on feature diversity and missing-mode coverage.
open_questions: What replaces finite-group irreps as the analyzable feature basis for natural language or vision data?
Can transition times and their scale dependence be derived without assuming clean separation of stages?
Does the same hidden-gradient energy predict which features emerge in transformers with normalization and residual streams?
Can prospective scaling tests distinguish the log(M)/M landscape-stability law from alternative grokking mechanisms?

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational empirical discovery of delayed generalization and its dependence on dataset size.
competitive_landscape.difference: Power et al. establish the phenomenon and empirical phase behavior; Li2 proposes a gradient-level feature mechanism and an explicit sample threshold for group tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Mechanistic three-stage account of Fourier-circuit formation in modular addition.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. reverse-engineer transformer circuits and define empirical progress measures; Li2 derives a staged process and feature landscape from shallow-network gradient dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct theoretical account of delayed feature learning following an initial kernel-like solution.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kumar et al. characterize a lazy-to-rich transition through sufficient statistics in polynomial regression and selected broader tasks; Li2 resolves individual group-theoretic features, interaction, and a sampling law.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as Dimensional Phase Transition in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Subsequent phase-transition explanation using gradient-avalanche effective dimensionality across model sizes.
competitive_landscape.difference: The later work measures a scale-dependent critical transition in gradient geometry, whereas Li2 predicts a structured feature landscape and data threshold from deterministic gradient dynamics.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a first-principles framework that identifies which features emerge, how hidden nodes interact, and why sample size and Muon change grokking, with provable scaling laws.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The novel core is the nonlinear-CCA energy plus complete group-irrep landscape and sampled-landscape stability law. The broad grokking narrative overlaps existing lazy-to-rich and three-stage accounts, and its reach beyond shallow group tasks is not yet demonstrated.

reviewer_notes: Read the full main text and theorem/experiment appendices across the 50-page extraction, including proof assumptions and hyperparameter discussions. Competitors and one post-publication adjacent theory were checked on primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
